learning_outcomes.text: Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability to manage information, handle and apply technical specifications and the necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
Knowledge and use of the principles of strength of materials.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Manufacturing Processes and Industry 4.0
Integration between design and manufacturing. DFM, design oriented to manufacturing.
Casting in disposable and permanent molds.
Visit to the mechanical workshop and CNC simulation.
teaching_methods: Presentation of theory and general examples

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (written exam)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises

assessment_rules: To pass, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be obtained in the final written exam. Attendance at all practical sessions is mandatory to pass the subject. The grading system follows RD 1125/2003 of September 5.
